parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no entry bar, no facility exclusion or registration regime is documented; same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2021 and orientation discrimination is punishable, though gender identity has no enumerated constitutional ground. Against that, the 2024 shadow report documents persistent discrimination in health, education and employment with under-investigated violence, and in June 2024 police attacked, injured and arbitrarily detained a transgender woman with degrading treatment — now under military-judicial investigation. No remedy is shown operating for a trans person, NGO capacity is thin, and border practice, custody placement and facilities are unsourced. Documented state-implicated police harm plus thin recourse places this below acceptance-with-working-remedies tier and above regimes with statutory ID-verification or entry-bar exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry or visa provision specific to trans travellers is recorded; the only entry-adjacent material is external asylum-packet and foreign travel-advice links. Whether officers treat a foreign marker or mismatch adversely is unsourced.
entry_documents.interaction: Arrival-stage risk is an open question rather than a documented restriction; the visitor's documents are home-issued and no local marker process applies at the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: June 2024: a transgender woman was attacked by police because of her gender identity, physically injured, arbitrarily detained and subjected to degrading treatment. No data on birth-sex versus identity placement, units or segregation for trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The case is under investigation by the judicial military police.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An outed visitor entering custody would face unknown placement rules and a force with a recent documented record of identity-motivated abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No shelters, safe houses or gender-neutral facilities are recorded; the record states absence of a record is not evidence of absence.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access for an outed visitor is unresolved; no institutional practice on gendered accommodation is described.

care_services.exposure: The 2024 shadow report documents persistent discrimination in health services against LGBTQI+ people, with no itemised incidents, dates or outcomes.
care_services.protection: People living with HIV/AIDS are legally entitled to health care and protection from employment discrimination; general Title II privacy and dignity provisions apply.
care_services.interaction: Trans-specific care access is not separately addressed; entitlement runs through general and HIV-specific provisions rather than identity grounds.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 23 of the constitution does not enumerate gender or sexual orientation; anti-discrimination protection covers orientation, not gender identity, so a trans visitor's claim rests on general provisions. No law permits gender-marker change.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same-sex conduct decriminalised from 11 February 2021; orientation discrimination in employment and services punishable by up to two years.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The statutory package reaches orientation only; gender-identity discrimination falls through to general rights with no documented enforcement practice.

minors_guardians.interaction: No youth- or minor-specific findings on travel, medication or education appear in the inventory.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Violence against LGBTQI+ people is documented as under-investigated, alongside a 2024 police assault on a transgender woman; no violence counts or homicide baseline allow magnitude assessment.
street_violence_police_response.protection: The police assault is under investigation by the judicial military police, implying some oversight mechanism operates.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are both the documented perpetrator in one case and the body a victim must approach; recourse is untested for trans complainants.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No demonstrated remedy secured by a trans person; one of two LGBT groups is legally recognised (2018, ~200 members), funding for the 2006-founded association unavailable, education work underfunded.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Criminal liability for orientation discrimination and general constitutional complaint routes exist on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin civil-society capacity and untested identity claims mean a visitor would have little practical support to pursue a complaint.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra maintains a Visitor Conduct Register barring noncompliant trans visitors with routine, universal enforcement and no effective remedy. This jurisdiction records no entry-bar mechanism at all, so its traveller-facing exposure is materially lighter despite comparable absence of remedy.

Kestrel Isles documents systematic border secondary screening, refused admission and administrative removal for document divergence. Here border practice is entirely unsourced, so that administrative exposure is absent — but this dossier has a documented 2024 police assault with degrading treatment, a severity Kestrel's account lacks, roughly offsetting it.

Meridia has trained border officers, a tribunal hearing appeals, written reasons, counsel access and compensation for unlawful holding. No equivalent remedy is shown operating here for a trans person, and the recent custodial abuse was not followed by documented relief, placing this materially below that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a statute book without trans-specific restrictions joined to institutions that do not reliably deliver: decriminalisation and an orientation-only anti-discrimination provision on one side, an unenumerated constitutional ground, no gender-recognition route, documented service discrimination and a recent police assault on a transgender woman on the other. No universal-exposure measure — entry bar, registration, facility exclusion, marker disclosure — appears in the record, which keeps the case clear of the severe tier. The absence of any documented working remedy, plus state-implicated abuse under investigation rather than remedied, holds it in the elevated band rather than above it; border, custody-placement and facility practice remain genuine but unresolved questions.
